name: Executive Order of April 28, 1864 for a mill and timber reserve on the Truckee River for the Pyramid Lake Paiute
nations: Washoe Tribe (the reserve lay in Washoe country, per Royce)
promises: Not a treaty: a presidential order. It established a mill and timber reserve on the Truckee River at the California line for the use of the Pyramid Lake reservation Indians; Royce gives its area as 20,531.38 acres.
today: Royce records that the reserve was surveyed but never used for its purpose, that the Indian Office lost sight of it so that in 1870 Agent Douglass reported no such reservation existed, and that it was tacitly abandoned without any formal relinquishment. That is the government's record of the reserve lapsing; it is not a finding that the Paiute were wronged, so it is not counted as a breach here.

sources.title: Royce, Schedule of Indian Land Cessions, 1864 entries (cession 460)
sources.publisher: Bureau of American Ethnology, 18th Annual Report, part 2 (Royce, Indian Land Cessions, 1899), Internet Archive

openQuestions: Whether the Northern Paiute (Docket 87 or 87-A) or Washoe (Docket 288) claims before the Indian Claims Commission covered the timber reserve was not checked.
Royce says the Secretary of the Interior told the General Land Office on July 13, 1864 that the President had ordered the reserve; the April 28, 1864 date is from Royce's date column.
